youtube.title: MONEY TALKS
youtube.summary: Paul Brennan speaks with Louis Boulanger of LB Now about a looming sovereign debt crisis across the G7 and the prospect of financial repression as governments struggle with rising debt-servicing costs. They explore Judy Shelton’s proposal for long-term US Treasury bonds redeemable in gold, the growing role of gold in global reserves, China’s monetary ambitions and whether the world is heading towards a major monetary reset. DISCLAIMER: The views and information shared on this show are for educational and informational purposes only. They do not constitute personalised financial, investment, tax, or legal advice. Listeners should seek guidance from a licensed financial professional who can provide advice based on their individual situation. youtube.title: Vote Smart 2026: The 'Overhang' & Strategic Voting Explained
youtube.summary: OVERHANGS. STRATEGIC VOTING. TWO VOTES. ONE LOLLY SCRAMBLE. 🍬 www.VoteSmart2026.co.nz Heard strategic voting mentioned approximately 4,000 times lately but still not entirely sure how it works? Wondering what an overhang is, why Parliament can suddenly sprout extra MPs, or how using your two votes differently could change the final numbers? Excellent. We bought lollies. In just a few minutes, we explain the whole thing using jellybeans, M&Ms, gummy teeth, Froot Loops, blackballs, gummy bears and a suspiciously important collection of chocolate bullets. No political science degree required. Just two votes, some very peculiar maths, and 120 seats that don't necessarily stay 120. Watch The Lolly Scramble, then head to www.VoteSmart2026.co.nz to learn more about how your two votes work. And share this with someone who still thinks an overhang is something requiring Spanx. 😜 Authorised by NZ Media Holdings 2023 Ltd (RCR Media), ContactUs@rcr.media

youtube.title: TWO BLOKES & A BOT
youtube.summary: Rodney Hide and software developer Tauriq Barron explore how rapidly AI is reshaping work, education and everyday life, questioning whether politicians and institutions are keeping pace. They discuss AI’s impact on software developers, the lack of coherent political policy on AI in education, and proposed regulation that could entrench the biggest technology companies. Rodney also reflects on using AI for unexpectedly rich theological conversations. youtube.title: WINSTON PETERS
youtube.summary: With the 2026 election just four weeks away, Paul Brennan speaks with New Zealand First leader and Foreign Minister Winston Peters about the latest polling, media coverage, immigration-system failures and concerns over digital ID. Peters also discusses the need for economic growth, a further Covid inquiry and his party’s remaining campaign policies, arguing that New Zealand needs greater ambition and a clearer path to recovery. youtube.title: DR ERIC CRAMPTON
youtube.summary: With the election looming, New Zealand Initiative chief economist Eric Crampton joins Paul Brennan to assess an EU complaint over New Zealand’s environmental policies, Labour’s proposed student loan write-offs and National’s plan to break up the major supermarkets. Crampton argues the trade complaint poses little immediate risk, while questioning the economic logic of loan write-offs and warning that supermarket reform should tackle regulatory barriers and property-rights concerns first.
